messages: Alex Nguyen: Quick q — want to lock down expected behavior for job cancellation + polling backoff. Current endpoints: POST /v1/jobs (returns request_id), GET /v1/jobs/:id (status payload), POST /v1/jobs/:id/cancel. Questions: 1) when client calls cancel while job is running, should server return 200 with updated final state or 202 with an in-progress cancelling state? 2) what fields should we add to status responses to help clients (e.g., cancellable, grace_period_ms)? 3) recommended client polling/backoff strategy? Trying to make this non-breaking for existing clients. :thinking:

Alex Nguyen: Quick q — want to lock down expected behavior for job cancellation + polling backoff. Current endpoints: POST /v1/jobs (returns request_id), GET /v1/jobs/:id (status payload), POST /v1/jobs/:id/cancel. Questions: 1) when client calls cancel while job is running, should server return 200 with updated final state or 202 with an in-progress cancelling state? 2) what fields should we add to status responses to help clients (e.g., cancellable, grace_period_ms)? 3) recommended client polling/backoff strategy? Trying to make this non-breaking for existing clients. :thinking:

Maria Park: TL;DR — make cancel best-effort and non-blocking: return 202 Accepted with a short body that transitions the job into a `cancelling` state. Include optional metadata fields so clients can make smarter decisions. Example: `POST /v1/jobs/:id/cancel` -> 202 body:

```json
{
  "request_id": "abc123",
  "status": "cancelling",
  "cancellable": true,
  "grace_period_ms": 5000,
  "message": "Cancellation requested; worker has 5s to tear down gracefully."
}
```

If the job cannot be cancelled (e.g., short non-interruptible kernel op), return 200 with the current state and `"cancellable": false` and a reason. Repeated cancel calls must be idempotent (same result). :white_check_mark:

Jordan Lee: +1 to 202 + `cancelling`. Also propose we standardize allowed status strings to avoid client parsing surprises: `queued`, `running`, `cancelling`, `cancelled`, `succeeded`, `failed`. Transition rules: queued -> running -> (succeeded|failed|cancelling). If `cancelling` completes the final state becomes `cancelled` (or `failed` if cleanup failed). Add an optional `last_transition_ts` for clients that need to display progress, but make it optional (non-breaking).

Maria Park: On backward compatibility: only add optional fields. `status` (string) stays mandatory. New fields: `cancellable` (boolean), `grace_period_ms` (int), `message` (string), `last_transition_ts` (int) — all optional. Clients that only read `status` keep working. Make sure to document semantics in the API reference and in the migration notes.

Jordan Lee: Server-side timeouts: default job TTL = 5 minutes, configurable per queue/model. Cancellation grace window default = 5s (from Maria example), but make configurable via queue config. Also important: when we accept a cancel we should publish a cancel event on the internal bus so workers spinning up can receive it ASAP. For jobs that are CPU/GPU-bound and uninterruptible, workers should still report `cancellable: false` in the status so UI can indicate it.

Chen Wu: Small note on request_id lifecycle: keep status record for 24 hours (retention) for debugging and client retrieval. After TTL, GET should return 404. That avoids unbounded DB retention. Also recommend `X-Request-ID` in responses to aid tracing.
deploy-bot: deployed job-worker v2 to staging (default grace_period_ms=5000) :rocket:

Alex Nguyen: This is great, thanks. I'll update the API doc with the suggested schema and add a small example showing both a successful cancel (202 -> cancelling -> cancelled) and a non-cancellable case (200 with `"cancellable": false`). One open question: do we want `cancelling` to appear on the job list endpoints or only on individual GET? Leaning to exposing it everywhere (so UI can show live cancellation). Thoughts?

Maria Park: Expose `cancelling` in list results too — clients should be able to show progress in dashboards. Keep the list payload compact (no heavy metadata) but include `status` and `cancellable` where known.
Jordan Lee: I'll add unit tests for idempotent cancel + state transitions and an integration test to verify Retry-After handling. Chen, can you add docs for polling best-practices?

Chen Wu: On it. I'll draft a small snippet for the SDKs with built-in poller using the backoff params above. Will also add a note recommending server-sent events/websockets for UI clients that need low-latency updates (polling is for simple consumers).
Alex Nguyen: perfect — thanks everyone. I'll send the API PR and tag y'all for review. :pray:
